LESSON: SAFETY ON RAISED PLATFORMS

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES
Strand: Foundations of Pre – Technical Studies
Topic 1.1: Safety on Raised Platforms

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Safety on Raised Platforms. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: when working on raised platforms. What is the importance of observing safety when working on raised platforms?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify types of raised platforms used in performing tasks
2. describe risks associated with working on raised platforms
3. observe safety when working on raised platforms
4. appreciate the need for observing safety while working on raised platforms

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: SAFETY ON RAISED PLATFORMS
Subject: PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Safety on Raised Platforms helps you succeed in PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in the workshop corner, classroom, or a safe practice space.

KEY FACTS: SAFETY ON RAISED PLATFORMS
Study Safety on Raised Platforms like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Identify types of raised platforms used in performing tasks

What this means
In this part you learn to identify types of raised platforms used in performing tasks. You will use ideas from in the workshop corner, classroom, or a safe practice space.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify types of raised platforms used in performing tasks.
2. Plan safely, do the steps, then check using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Safety first: State one safety rule before practising “Safety on Raised Platforms”.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify types of raised platforms used in performing tasks. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Describe risks associated with working on raised platforms

What this means
In this part you learn to describe risks associated with working on raised platforms. You will use ideas from in the workshop corner, classroom, or a safe practice space.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe risks associated with working on raised platforms.
2. Plan safely, do the steps, then check using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Steps: List 3 correct steps to complete a simple task on Safety on Raised Platforms.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe risks associated with working on raised platforms. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Observe safety when working on raised platforms

What this means
In this part you learn to observe safety when working on raised platforms. You will use ideas from in the workshop corner, classroom, or a safe practice space.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: observe safety when working on raised platforms.
2. Plan safely, do the steps, then check using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Check: Inspect your work and say one improvement.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can observe safety when working on raised platforms. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Appreciate the need for observing safety while working on raised platforms

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the need for observing safety while working on raised platforms. You will use ideas from in the workshop corner, classroom, or a safe practice space.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the need for observing safety while working on raised platforms.
2. Plan safely, do the steps, then check using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Safety first: State one safety rule before practising “Safety on Raised Platforms”.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the need for observing safety while working on raised platforms. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Safety on Raised Platforms is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: State one safety rule before practising “Safety on Raised Platforms”. (skill: identify types of raised platforms used in performing tasks)

Example 2: List 3 correct steps to complete a simple task on Safety on Raised Platforms. (skill: describe risks associated with working on raised platforms)

Example 3: Inspect your work and say one improvement. (skill: observe safety when working on raised platforms)

Example 4: State one safety rule before practising “Safety on Raised Platforms”. (skill: appreciate the need for observing safety while working on raised platforms)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Safety on Raised Platforms to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify types of raised platforms used in performing tasks.
3. Practise this skill: describe risks associated with working on raised platforms.
4. Practise this skill: observe safety when working on raised platforms.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Safety on Raised Platforms from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Safety on Raised Platforms: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Safety on Raised Platforms?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. when working on raised platforms. What is the importance of observing safety when working on raised platforms?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Safety on Raised Platforms means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify types of raised platforms used in performing tasks.
5. Be able to: describe risks associated with working on raised platforms.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
